page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.8xlarge is an x86_64 server instance within the Local SSDs family, managed via the KVM hypervisor. Hardware resources include 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each core supports two threads and provides 32 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache, backed by 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI alongside AES and BMI2. The instance bundles 256 GB of system RAM, yielding 8 GB per vCPU, and integrates 7679 GB of local SSD storage paired with a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

Benchmark assessments position the instance in the middle tier for multi-threaded computation, with a PassMark CPU score of 27316.39 and Geekbench multi-core score of 10415.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 113.07 GB/sec on large uncached reads and 49.34 GB/sec on large writes, supporting data-intensive operations such as Redis at 28.0 million operations per second. However, single-core capabilities reflect limitations of the 2.5 GHz base clock; single-core stress-ng metrics fall into the bottom 25 percent, and single-threaded gzip compression performs at 23.03 GB/sec. For machine learning inference on CPU, small 135M parameter models achieve 1458.16 tokens per second during prompt processing, while medium 7B models yield 42.17 tokens per second.

The bundled integration of 7679 GB local SSD storage and 256 GB RAM provides high resource density for operations constrained by I/O throughput. The instance profile favors applications requiring localized disk persistence and high memory capacities without relying on separate network-attached storage. Best-fit workloads include distributed databases such as Apache Cassandra and MongoDB, high-capacity relational database engines, Elasticsearch clusters, and analytical ETL pipelines requiring fast local scratch space.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.8xlarge is a storage- and memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, it supplies 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by 35 MB of Level 3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance incorporates 256 GB of RAM alongside 7679 GB of integrated local SSD storage, delivering substantial data density without reliance on external network volumes. Its network throughput maintains a baseline of 10 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks show average multi-core compute and memory performance, though single-core execution speeds fall into the lower quartile. The architecture trades peak single-thread frequency for high parallel throughput and dense local disk capacity. Consequently, this configuration operates efficiently for I/O-intensive workloads, including high-scale relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, Elasticsearch clusters, in-memory key-value stores like Redis, and data transformation pipelines requiring fast local scratch disks.
